chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in Yemen regarding a people whose house collapsed upon them, leaving two boys: one a slave and the other free. He cast lots between them, and the lot fell on one of them, so he gave the wealth to that one and freed the other.
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided when a slave and a free person die simultaneously in a collapsed house?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, illustrates Imam Ali’s (AS) application of *al-khums* (casting lots) in the Yemeni case of simultaneous death (*al-mutawaffayn*), where the identity of the free heir versus the slave was unknown. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that in cases of indistinguishable simultaneous death, the presumption of freedom is not automatically applied to both, but rather determined by chance to preserve the integrity of inheritance shares. The narrative underscores the practical wisdom of the Imam in resolving complex inheritance disputes with equity and precision.
